top.title: Texas Rep. Files Bill Letting Cities Invest $10 Million in Bitcoin
top.description: Bitcoin Magazine Texas Rep. Files Bill Letting Cities Invest $10 Million in Bitcoin A Texas lawmaker filed a bill Monday that would let each city and county in the state invest up to $10 million of public money in bitcoin or another cryptocurrency, without setting any rules for how those coins would be held. House Bill 815, filed by Rep. Ron Reynolds, a Missouri City Democrat, on the first day of prefiling for the 90th Texas Legislature, carries the caption “Relating to the authority of a municipality or county to invest money in cryptocurrencies.” The introduced text , posted on the Texas Legislature’s site, is two sections long. The bill would amend the Public Funds Investment Act, Chapter 2256 of the Texas Government Code, by adding a new Section 2256.0165, titled “Authorized Investments: Cryptocurrency.” Under that section, “a municipality or county may invest not more than $10 million of its money or money under its control in Bitcoin or another cryptocurrency.” The authority would take effect Sept. 1, 2027, if the bill becomes law. The $10 million figure is a cap on each city or county, not a single statewide pool. School districts and other local governments covered by the investment act are left out. What the bill does and does not say The measure borrows its definitions of “Bitcoin” and “cryptocurrency” from Section 403.701 of the Government Code, the definitions written into law last year by Senate Bill 21, which created the Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve . Bitcoin is defined as a decentralized cryptocurrency created by a peer-to-peer network that operates independently of any central authority or bank. Cryptocurrency is defined more broadly as a virtual currency that uses cryptography to secure transactions recorded on a distributed ledger, such as a blockchain. That means a city or county would not be limited to bitcoin. The bill also does not import the reserve law’s requirement that coins bought for the state fund have an average market capitalization of at least $500 billion over the most recent 24-month period, or its provisions on cold storage and qualified custodians. The Public Funds Investment Act already requires local governments to adopt a written investment policy that emphasizes safety of principal and liquidity, and to invest with the care a prudent person would use in managing their own affairs. A city or county would still have to add cryptocurrency to that policy before buying any. The new section itself is silent on custody, on audits specific to digital assets, and on how a loss would be handled. A narrower version of last year’s proposal Reynolds filed a broader measure, House Bill 4258, on March 10, 2025, with Rep. Mihaela Plesa. That bill would have let the comptroller invest as much as $250 million of the Economic Stabilization Fund, the state’s rainy day fund, in bitcoin or another cryptocurrency, and it included the same $10 million cap for cities and counties. top.title: Undefeated Middletown football team out of Section 9 final due to eligibility issue
top.description: Middletown has been removed from the Section 9 Class AA football playoffs after it was forced to forfeit its semifinal win due to an eligibility issue. (Jim Franco/Times Union) (Jim Franco/Times Union) An issue surrounding the use of an ineligible player has thrown the Section 9 Class AA football playoffs into chaos ahead of this weekend's sectional championships. Middletown, which boasted an undefeated record after its sectional semifinal win over Valley Central this past weekend, had been scheduled to face Newburgh Free Academy for the Section 9 title this coming Saturday, but has since forfeited that win for using an ineligible player. According to a letter posted to the Enlarged City School District of Middletown's website signed by superintendent Amy Creeden and athletic director Justin Sturge, in the aftermath of Middletown's 48-15 win over Valley Central, "a question was raised regarding whether one of our varsity football players met postseason eligibility requirements." After reviewing the situation with Section 9 officials, it was confirmed that the unidentified player did not meet the minimum requirement of participating in three regular-season games to be eligible for the postseason. The letter called the issue an "unintentional adult error in understanding the rules," and the district immediately requested a waiver from Section 9, which was denied. The district then appealed to the state high school athletic association, but the appeal was also denied. Due to the forfeit, Middletown's record has been dropped to 9-1 and Valley Central has been inserted into Saturday's Section 9 Class AA final against Newburgh. "We want to be very clear: this was an error made by adults, not our scholars," the letter reads. "Not one student-athlete did anything wrong." In a statement to the Times Union, NYSPHSAA Executive Director Robert Zayas said: "NYSPHSAA recognizes the disappointment and frustration surrounding the circumstances involving the Middletown varsity football program, particularly for the student-athletes who have worked hard throughout an outstanding season. "The rules and eligibility standards of NYSPHSAA are established and approved by our member schools through the Association's formal governance process. As Executive Director, my authority is defined by the NYSPHSAA Constitution and Handbook, and any exceptions to established rules must be consistent with the provisions approved by our membership. "While we recognize the circumstances surrounding this violation, NYSPHSAA has a responsibility to ensure the consistent and equitable application of its rules and eligibility standards across all member schools. According to the letter on the district website, the Middletown school district "is actively working with legal counsel to pursue further legal recourse on our team's behalf. top.title: Grade the trade: Vikings get a throwback QB, deal with Raiders for old friend Kirk Cousins
top.description: After Monday night, the Minnesota Vikings knew they had to try to get a quarterback. They landed a familiar face. The Vikings traded for Kirk Cousins, who spent six of his 15 NFL seasons in Minnesota. They sent a third-round pick to the Raiders for the 38-year-old quarterback, via ESPN . That should start the Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas, while giving the Vikings hope for fixing their offense and winning the NFC North. Here are the grades for the trade: Vikings trade for Kirk Cousins Usually, viable quarterbacks aren’t available in trade. Credit to the Vikings for getting a deal done. After Minnesota watched Carson Wentz flounder around on Monday night, and after the team realized Kyler Murray wouldn’t be the answer, a bold move was needed. Cousins has played pretty well this season, with 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. He can come right in and run Kevin O’Connell’s offense, which made him more valuable to Minnesota than some other teams. Kirk Cousins is coming back to the Vikings for a second stint with the team. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) Thearon W. Henderson via Getty Images The Vikings weren’t going to be a Super Bowl contender with a treacherous quarterback situation. Cousins might not completely change that — he’s still by far the fourth-best quarterback in a tough division — but it’s well worth the price of a third-round pick to find out. Grade: B Raiders get a valuable pick The Raiders played the Kirk Cousins/Fernando Mendoza situation perfectly, as it turns out. They paid Cousins and gave him the first nine games of the season. With the Raiders slipping to 4-5 and their playoff hopes becoming more unrealistic, it was about time to turn the offense over to Mendoza anyway. So the Raiders paid for half of a season from Cousins and got a third-round pick out of it in the end. That’s really smart business. The Raiders might have Aidan O’Connell start for a few games if they truly don’t think Mendoza, the first overall pick, is ready. Either way, Las Vegas was playing chess with how it got a valuable top-100 pick for a 38-year-old quarterback who was probably going to start only a few more games anyway. Grade: A

top.title: Real Madrid eye 24-year-old Brighton ace as potential replacement for veteran superstar – report
top.description: Real Madrid eye 24-year-old Brighton ace as potential replacement for veteran superstar – report According to TeamTalk (h/t Bernabeu Digital ), Real Madrid have identified Brighton & Hove Albion goalkeeper Bart Verbruggen as a potential replacement for veteran superstar Thibaut Courtois. The Spanish capital club are closely monitoring the Netherlands international’s progress as they begin planning for the long-term future of their goalkeeping position. Courtois still remains a key figure Courtois remains a key figure at Real Madrid and continues to be an important part of Jose Mourinho’s squad at the Santiago Bernabeu. At 34 years old, the Belgian shot-stopper continues to remain one of the best goalkeepers in the business. In the ongoing season, he has played 15 appearances across all competitions, keeping four clean sheets and conceding 16 goals. His performances have been clutch in the team maintaining an impressive run of form under Mourinho. Still a key figure at Real Madrid. (Photo by Juan Manuel Serrano Arce/Getty Images) While his current contract expires in 2027, a new one-year extension is already in the works for the veteran goalkeeper. However, Real Madrid are already laying the groundwork for life beyond their ace goalkeeper as they wish to be prepared with a succession plan rather than searching for a replacement when it becomes an immediate necessity. Bart Verbruggen the chosen one? As such, Real Madrid have identified Verbruggen as their most preferred candidate to take over from Courtois in the long run. The 24-year-old Dutchman’s age, physical presence, reliability between the posts and ability to contribute to build-up play make him an appealing option. Verbruggen’s contract expires in 2028. (Photo by Naomi Baker/Getty Images) Meanwhile, as per the report, the Netherlands goalkeeper would find it difficult to turn down a concrete offer from Real Madrid. However, the biggest obstacle for Los Blancos will be the position taken by Brighton & Hove Albion. They do not want to let go of the 24-year-old and see him as a key part of their project. But the summer of 2027 could provide a window of opportunity for Real Madrid. Verbruggen’s contract with the Seagulls expires in 2028, meaning he would be entering the final year of his deal at the end of the current season. If a new contract is not negotiated, he could become available for a reasonable price and Brighton could be forced to sell in order to avoid losing him for free when his deal runs out.

top.title: 49ers add wide receiver Keenan Allen in trade with Colts as deadline approaches
top.description: Indianapolis Colts wide receiver Keenan Allen (10) catches a pass in front of Dallas Cowboys' Malik Hooker (24) andn Daron Bland (26) during the first half of an NFL football game in Indianapolis, Sunday, Nov. 8, 2026. (AP Photo/Jeff Roberson) (Jeff Roberson/Associated Press) On Tuesday, two weeks after the San Francisco 49ers acquired a 30-something from the Colts, they acquired another 30-something from Indianapolis in an all-in Super Bowl push. The 49ers traded a 2027 sixth-round pick to the Colts for wide receiver Keenan Allen, 34, after dealing a 2027 fourth-rounder to Indianapolis for defensive tackle DeForest Buckner, 32, a league source said. The 49ers have five picks in next year's draft: a first-, second-, third-, fifth- and seventh-rounder. With the 49ers dealing with a host of wide receiver injuries, most notably to six-time Pro Bowl selection Mike Evans, they dealt for Allen, a six-time Pro Bowl pick who has 40 catches for 351 yards and a touchdown in eight games this season. Allen, a 14-year veteran who attended Cal, is an elite route-runner who ranks second among active players in receptions (1,095), fourth in receiving yards (12,402) and fifth in receiving touchdowns (71). Allen, of course, is in his career twilight. The 49ers will be his fourth team since he was traded from the Chargers to the Bears for a fourth-round pick in March 2024. Since his last Pro Bowl season in 2023, he has 191 catches for 1,872 yards and 12 touchdowns in 40 games, averaging 9.8 yards per catch. Sporting a 7-1 record, the 49ers grabbed Allen about two hours before Tuesday's 1 p.m. trade deadline with Evans, 33, dealing with Achilles tendinitis that's sidelined him since he was forced to exit a win against the Commanders on Oct. 19. top.title: Video catches USC announcer's take on targeting call
top.description: He said what? That’s what many were asking regarding longtime USC football radio play-by-play announcer Pete Arbogast’s reaction to Oregon quarterback Dante Moore being knocked out of Saturday’s 41-27 Ducks’ victory at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. The play occurred in the second quarter when Moore scrambled and slid. USC linebacker Desman Stephens II then put his shoulder into Moore’s head, knocking him backward into the turf. Moore lay on the field for several minutes before being taken off on a cart and loaded into an ambulance. Stephens celebrated the hit even after being flagged, leading to a skirmish with several Oregon players. Meanwhile, up in the radio booth, Arbogast said the play did not appear to be targeting and claimed Moore didn’t slide feet-first. Arbogast went on to claim that Stephens went in helmet first and ran into Moore who “ducked into that hit.” “I saw him dive forward,” Arbogast claimed. Radio analyst Shaun Cody, who played defensive line at USC (2001-2004) and spent eight seasons in the NFL (Detroit and Houston), clearly disagreed. “He’s laying feet first,” Cody responded. But Arbogast countered, “Well, he is now because they spun him around.” Cody disagreed again, and Arbogast said he wanted to see the replay, which clearly showed Moore sliding feet-first and Stephens going in head-first, with his right shoulder striking Moore in the head. “Yeah, not a feet-first slide, it’s more of a knee slide,” Arbogast claimed while watching the replay. While it’s one thing not to see clearly a live play from high up in a radio booth, it’s another to watch the replay and claim to see something that didn’t exist. Footage from the USC radio team in the Oregon game 😂😂😂 i can’t believe this is real pic.twitter.com/82HYans8Y9 — Adam Breneman (@AdamBreneman81) September 29, 2026 Cody immediately smirked at Arbogast’s viewpoint; then Arbogast added, “It didn’t look like targeting on the replay to us.” In response, Cody looked directly into the camera, eyes wide, and nodded, clearly disagreeing with Arbogast’s assessment. Homerism? Maybe. Potential advertising fodder for local optometrists to encourage thousands to update their eyeglass prescriptions? Absolutely. Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola replaced Moore and passed for 289 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Moore was later diagnosed with a concussion; he has entered concussion protocol and will be out indefinitely . Moore released a statement saying he would soon return. No. 15 Oregon (3-1, 1-0 Big Ten) hosts No. 23 UCLA (4-0, 2-0) at 12:30 p.m. on Oct. 10. top.title: Damian Lillard is back and Ja Morant is here. How exactly is this going to work? | Bill Oram
top.description: In the history of basketball, we have certainly seen some why-would-they-do-that? pairings. Jerseys and sleeves. Kawhi Leonard and a tree sponsorship. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Because of all the things you might have said the Trail Blazers needed as they prepared to welcome Lillard back after making a playoff run without him, a slight-of-stature ball-dominant guard with a questionable jump shot would not have topped anyone’s list. Depth on the wing? Yes. Shooting? Definitely. Defense? Always. Morant doesn’t particularly address any of those, and yet, he’s here, a dynamic two-time All-Star in need of a second act, being paid a team-high $42.1 million to play the same position as not just Lillard, but Jrue Holiday and Scoot Henderson. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. It’s happening. “It’s easy for people to be like, ‘Man how is this going to work,’” Lillard offered. “‘They can’t do this, they can’t do that.’ But being on the floor with them … we can be a dangerous team and I really believe that.” The onus is on the Trail Blazers starting this month to prove that they bet right in acquiring Morant. And that pairing him with Lillard isn’t the boondoggle conventional wisdom suggests it will be. Lillard noted how many teams that succeeded in the playoffs last year, think San Antonio with its four point guards, relied on numerous playmakers. To his credit, Morant said he would be comfortable coming off the bench, if necessary. But they would not be the first NBA team to fall into the trap of believing they are capable of adjusting or that they will be comfortable sacrificing. It isn’t uncommon to see players in those situations default to familiar habits and sensibilities once the season is underway or struggles come. That’s what made a lot of the positive energy around what sure seems like an awkward roster ring so hollow. We’re going to need to see it to believe it. top.description: On Tuesday, Detroit Red Wings interim general manager Shawn Horcoff attended his first NHL general managers meeting in Toronto. He is still carrying two difficult situations into it: Dylan Larkin is suspended without pay after leaving the team on Oct. 29, and Simon Edvinsson is still an unsigned restricted free agent. Horcoff would still rather sign Edvinsson than move him. Asked whether the standoff could soften that position, he told Nicholas J. Cotsonika of NHL.com , “I’d still like to sign Simon, but I think when it’s someone like that and the situation that we’re in, you can’t help but take calls. It’s my job to do what’s in the best interest of the Detroit Red Wings. I’m going to take all those calls and hear what people have to say.” Apr 11, 2026; Detroit, Michigan, USA; New Jersey Devils left wing Brian Halonen (48) skates with the puck defended by Detroit Red Wings center Andrew Copp (18) and defenseman Simon Edvinsson (77) in the third period at Little Caesars Arena. top.description: Real Madrid star opens the door to January exit Real Madrid star Endrick has admitted that he has not yet ruled out the possibility of departing Spain’s capital on loan during the winter transfer window. This comes amid a fresh round of speculation surrounding the name of the Brazilian international. Frontman Endrick has reemerged as a prominent figure in the transfer chatter across much of Europe over the last 24 hours. Amid a search for mid-season reinforcements up top, Premier League champions Arsenal are understood to have earmarked the 20-year-old as a potential loan signing. Endrick has continued to struggle for game-time at Real Madrid this season, despite being repeatedly backed by manager José Mourinho in public. Speaking during an exchange with the media on Tuesday, the young attacker was himself therefore drawn on the prospect of a 2nd successive winter loan move. top.description: We’ve reached NFL and therefore Seattle Seahawks trade deadline week, which often promises to have some interesting deals and rarely actually materializes. Minor or mid-level deals have happened more recently on deadline day itself, so it’s not like we live in a “nothing happens” world. There have admittedly been prominent in-season trades already this year, including the Quenton Nelson and Jeffery Simmons trades just a couple of weeks ago, as well as Joey Porter Jr going to the Dallas Cowboys, and Marvin Harrison Jr heading for the Houston Texans. top.title: 76ers Undefeated In Clutch, But This Streak Is A Trap
top.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images The Philadelphia 76ers have won every single close game they have played this season, but that perfect record might be the biggest problem they face. The team improved to 9-2 on the season after beating the Chicago Bulls 127-121 on Sunday, a victory that kept their clutch record at a flawless 8-0. While fans love the drama, the reality is that a roster full of aging stars cannot survive this much stress week after week. The 76ers have played eight clutch games so far, which is the most in the entire league by a wide margin, according to The Sixer Sense . LeBron James has a clear explanation for why the team stays cool when the clock winds down. He told reporters after the win that the squad simply does not panic under pressure. “We have a lot of guys that’s been in late-game situations, and we have a no-panic button,” James said. He added that the group understands they must get stops, but they also know how to stay calm if the other team goes on a run. This mindset has worked so far, but it masks a deeper issue with how the team plays for the full 48 minutes. The Danger of Constant Comebacks Winning tight games is a great trait to have, yet relying on it every night is a recipe for exhaustion. According to The Sixer Sense , the 76ers have recovered from deficits to secure victories far too frequently this season, even versus inferior opponents. top.title: Here’s What Malik Nabers Revealed After Fox Criticized His Attitude
top.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers has entered a heated public dispute with Fox Sports broadcasters following the team’s 19-11 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. During the game, play-by-play announcer Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen criticized Nabers for his demeanor, with Davis stating the player’s body language “has been terrible today”. Nabers responded quickly on social media, taking to an Instagram story to call out the commentators for their assessment. Defending the Stoic Look The core of the argument centers on whether a player must show emotion to be a good teammate. Olsen had suggested that great receivers must demand the ball, noting, “There’s never been a great wide receiver who hasn’t demanded the ball”, according to ESPN . However, he also warned that being demanding should never hurt the team’s success. Nabers rejected the idea that his face changes based on the score. He insisted, “My face is the same way if I’m having a good game, bad, winning or losing”. Nabers clarified that his frustration was actually directed at his own team’s effort, not his teammates. He admitted he felt the offense was “lollygagging our way through the game”, according to Sports Illustrated . He explained that he was trying to “wake everybody up just to make sure we’re playing a game right now”. The receiver emphasized that in a division matchup, players must “go attack people, you have to go attack the game”. Coach Harbaugh Steps In Giants head coach John Harbaugh addressed the controversy during his media availability on Monday. He defended his player, pointing out that outsiders cannot see the full context of what happens on the field. Harbaugh asked, “If you really don’t know the person, or you don’t know the dynamic or you don’t know the circumstances or who the person’s talking to, how do you have any idea what the application is and how do you judge it?” The coach concluded that it is difficult for anyone outside the huddle to make a fair call on player behavior. nigeria.title: 2027: Avoid technicalities, treat electronic evidence rigorously, INEC charges tribunals
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Chairman of the Independent National Electoral Commission INEC, Professor Joash Amupitan SAN, has urged members of the 2027 Election Petition Tribunals to avoid technicalities that defeat substantive justice and to subject electronic evidence to rigorous scrutiny. He also told them to keep firm control of their courtrooms and let “truth of the ballot prevail”. According to the commission’s Daily Bulletin of Tuesday, Amupitan spoke on Monday in Abuja while delivering the Commission’s opening remarks at a three-day workshop for Justices of the Court of Appeal and members of the tribunals, held at the Body of Benchers Complex. The Court of Appeal organised the workshop under the theme “Election Tribunal as a Tool for Political Stability.” The INEC chairman said electoral litigation had grown more complex, with disputes now touching on voter accreditation, electronic transmission of results, technological failures and the integrity of digital records. On the Bimodal Voter Accreditation System BVAS and the INEC Result Viewing Portal (IReV), he said technology should neither be treated as infallible nor dismissed simply because the evidence is electronic. For businesses, content creators, and people researching social media trends, another question can be just as interesting: which accounts does that person choose to follow? Someone may publicly promote fashion, technology, or entertainment while following creators in entirely different fields. A business account may begin following emerging influencers long before announcing a collaboration. A public figure may gradually change the types of accounts appearing on their Following list. These observations can provide useful context, particularly when viewed over time. An Instagram following tracker helps organize changes to the accounts a public Instagram profile follows. Rather than relying on a single snapshot, tools such as Snoopreport record detected follows and unfollows across reporting periods. The results can support social media research, although they cannot explain why someone followed an account or reveal information that Instagram keeps private. Why Follower Counts Don’t Tell the Whole Story Follower numbers are among Instagram’s most visible statistics. They influence how people assess popularity, reach, and sometimes commercial value. Yet having a large audience doesn’t necessarily mean an account has a clearly defined set of interests or strong connections within a particular industry. The Following list offers a different perspective. Consider a technology commentator who starts following several artificial intelligence researchers, software companies, and digital policy organizations. Those additions may suggest topics worth investigating. Similarly, a lifestyle influencer who follows numerous local restaurants might be exploring a new content category. Neither example proves a professional plan or future collaboration. Following someone can reflect curiosity, personal connections, or temporary interest. Still, when researchers compare several observations across time, they may discover changes worth examining further. The Difference Between Following and Followers Before using an Instagram following tracker, it’s important to distinguish two commonly confused terms. For example, a creator may have 40,000 followers while following only 600 accounts. A following tracker focuses on changes within those 600 connections, not on identifying people who recently followed the creator. Instagram allows users to inspect the Following list of an accessible public profile. However, the list doesn’t provide a dependable chronological history of when each connection was added. Their profiles may feature carefully selected photographs, polished videos, and short biographies, but their everyday interactions with content can tell another story. A person who rarely posts about travel may regularly like photographs of unfamiliar destinations. A creator known for fashion might engage with technology tutorials, food videos, or sports content. These interactions can suggest topics that attract someone’s attention, even when they don’t appear on the person’s own profile. Someone might like a photograph because they admire the subject, appreciate the photography, support a friend, or agree with a message. business.title: Texas Rep. Files Bill Letting Cities Invest $10 Million in Bitcoin
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Texas Rep. Files Bill Letting Cities Invest $10 Million in Bitcoin A Texas lawmaker filed a bill Monday that would let each city and county in the state invest up to $10 million of public money in bitcoin or another cryptocurrency, without setting any rules for how those coins would be held. House Bill 815, filed by Rep. Ron Reynolds, a Missouri City Democrat, on the first day of prefiling for the 90th Texas Legislature, carries the caption “Relating to the authority of a municipality or county to invest money in cryptocurrencies.” The introduced text , posted on the Texas Legislature’s site, is two sections long. The bill would amend the Public Funds Investment Act, Chapter 2256 of the Texas Government Code, by adding a new Section 2256.0165, titled “Authorized Investments: Cryptocurrency.” Under that section, “a municipality or county may invest not more than $10 million of its money or money under its control in Bitcoin or another cryptocurrency.” The authority would take effect Sept. 1, 2027, if the bill becomes law. The $10 million figure is a cap on each city or county, not a single statewide pool. School districts and other local governments covered by the investment act are left out. What the bill does and does not say The measure borrows its definitions of “Bitcoin” and “cryptocurrency” from Section 403.701 of the Government Code, the definitions written into law last year by Senate Bill 21, which created the Texas Strategic Bitcoin Reserve . Bitcoin is defined as a decentralized cryptocurrency created by a peer-to-peer network that operates independently of any central authority or bank. Cryptocurrency is defined more broadly as a virtual currency that uses cryptography to secure transactions recorded on a distributed ledger, such as a blockchain. That means a city or county would not be limited to bitcoin. The bill also does not import the reserve law’s requirement that coins bought for the state fund have an average market capitalization of at least $500 billion over the most recent 24-month period, or its provisions on cold storage and qualified custodians. The Public Funds Investment Act already requires local governments to adopt a written investment policy that emphasizes safety of principal and liquidity, and to invest with the care a prudent person would use in managing their own affairs. A city or county would still have to add cryptocurrency to that policy before buying any. The new section itself is silent on custody, on audits specific to digital assets, and on how a loss would be handled. A narrower version of last year’s proposal Reynolds filed a broader measure, House Bill 4258, on March 10, 2025, with Rep. Mihaela Plesa. That bill would have let the comptroller invest as much as $250 million of the Economic Stabilization Fund, the state’s rainy day fund, in bitcoin or another cryptocurrency, and it included the same $10 million cap for cities and counties. business.title: Poland’s Parliament Votes 240-202 to Let Officials Freeze Crypto Before Court Review
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Poland’s Parliament Votes 240-202 to Let Officials Freeze Crypto Before Court Review Poland’s lower house of parliament voted 240-202 on Friday to let the interior minister freeze crypto assets, bank accounts and other property of people placed on a national sanctions list, before any court reviews the order. The Sejm, Poland’s lower house, passed the Act on Restrictive Measures at its 68th sitting, with one member abstaining and 17 not voting. The Senate received the bill Monday and has 30 days under Article 121 of the Constitution to adopt, amend or reject it, after which it would go to President Karol Nawrocki. The law, a government bill that also implements European Union sanctions rules, treats crypto assets as financial means that can be frozen, using the definition in the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets regulation. A freeze, as the text defines it, is meant to stop any movement, transfer, use or other change that would let the holder benefit from the assets. The freeze applies only to people and entities the interior minister adds to a public national list, either on the minister’s own initiative or at the request of agencies that include the financial watchdog, the central bank, the financial intelligence unit and the internal security service. Grounds include supporting a country already under EU sanctions, serious human rights abuses, or initiating or financing information manipulation that poses a serious threat to Poland’s national security. A listing on that last ground requires a showing of a real and serious threat to Poland’s interests, borders, security or elections. The bill carves out ordinary journalism, political speech and publishing, unless that activity is a knowing campaign of the kind the law describes. A freeze that starts before a judge weighs in The interior minister’s decision takes effect the day after it is posted in the ministry’s Public Information Bulletin and is immediately enforceable. There is no request to the minister to reconsider. A listed person may file a complaint with an administrative court, but the law says the decision remains in force until a judgment becomes final, and it sets aside the usual rule that would let a court pause a challenged order. The measures also bar making funds or property available to listed persons and can exclude them from public contracts. In some cases, the economy minister may appoint a temporary administrator to sell frozen assets or, under a separate order, take them over for the State Treasury. What the freeze would mean for bitcoin The Poland bill does not target ordinary bitcoin holders in Poland. It reaches crypto assets owned, held or under the control of people and firms on the sanctions list. business.title: Binance Warns iOS Flaw Could Expose Wallet Seed Phrases as Apple’s Latest iPhone Patch Stays Silent
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Warns iOS Flaw Could Expose Wallet Seed Phrases as Apple’s Latest iPhone Patch Stays Silent Binance warned iPhone users Tuesday that a publicly released iOS flaw could let malicious apps read files stored by other apps, including the seed phrases and private keys that control crypto wallets. “A vulnerability (worse_query) affecting iOS 26.7.1, 27.0.1, and 27.2 allows malicious apps to read local files from other apps, putting seed phrases, private keys, and login credentials at risk across the entire ecosystem,” the exchange wrote on X. “This is an iOS-level issue, not unique to Binance.” Binance told users to delete any apps installed from untrusted sources, such as sideloaded or manually signed IPA files, and to update iOS and every app to the latest official versions. Anyone who suspects a breach should move funds to a new wallet created on a clean device and reset all active login sessions, the exchange said. Neither Binance nor the researcher behind the flaw has reported any thefts tied to it. What worse_query does The bug is a sandbox escape. On iOS, each app is supposed to live in its own container that other apps cannot read. A researcher who posts as forcequitOS released worse_query on GitHub on Nov. 8, calling it “a zero-day sandbox escape for iOS 26 and 27, again.” It succeeds an earlier exploit, bad_query. The project’s README says it works on iOS 26.0 through 26.7.2 and on iOS 27.2, a wider range than the versions Binance named. It lists paths it can reach, including other apps’ data containers and shared app group folders. The researcher describes it as “a proof-of-concept for developers” that “isn’t useful by itself,” and stresses it is not a jailbreak. To use it, a developer has to build it into an app. That has already happened in at least one case. A day after the release, developer Christoph Kolbicz published a file manager built on worse_query that lets users browse and edit app data on iOS 27 without jailbreaking, which he said was tested on iOS 27.0.1. Blockchain security firm SlowMist called worse_query a container sandbox escape rather than a jailbreak. Its chief information security officer, who posts as 23pds, wrote that the flaw will not steal assets on its own. The risk comes when a user installs and runs an untrusted IPA that then reads other apps’ containers, and only if a wallet stores mnemonic phrases, keystores or WebView caches in plain text on the device. Apple’s iOS updates don’t mention it Apple shipped iOS 27.2.1 and iOS 26.7.3 on Nov. 9, a day after the proof of concept went public. Their security notes list fixes for AirPlay, Bluetooth pairing, brotli and other components, but neither names worse_query or describes a sandbox escape of this kind. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Miami-Dade County Now Accepts Bitcoin for Property Taxes Miami-Dade County Tax Collector Dariel Fernandez said Monday his office has begun accepting bitcoin for property tax payments, both online and in person, while converting every transaction into dollars before the money reaches the county. Fernandez announced the change in a statement on the Tax Collector’s website, calling it a way to give property owners another option without putting public funds into the asset. Payers can select a cryptocurrency option during online checkout or request it at the counter, then connect a supported exchange account or digital wallet and authorize the payment. A third-party system converts the bitcoin into U.S. dollars at the time of payment, the office said, so it never holds, invests in or manages any cryptocurrency. The office said it still receives the full dollar amount owed and records the transactions in its standard payment reports, without county workers maintaining digital wallets. “Government must keep up with the times and the needs of the people we serve,” Fernandez said. “By accepting Bitcoin as a payment option, we are giving property owners another way to pay their taxes, whether online or in person, while continuing to offer the traditional payment methods they already know and trust.” He added that the office is “embracing new technology without compromising our responsibility to protect taxpayer dollars.” Whether someone pays with bitcoin or a conventional method, he said, “our office receives the full amount owed in U.S. dollars.” The office did not name the payment processor or say whether bitcoin payments carry a convenience fee. Card and mobile-wallet payments already carry a nonrefundable 2.50% fee online, with a $2.50 minimum, the office’s payment-methods page shows. Traditional options, including checks, cards, cash and fee-free eChecks, remain available. The announcement covers property taxes, and the option is voluntary. Miami-Dade opened the 2026 tax roll on Oct. 30 and is urging owners to pay by Nov. 30 to lock in a 4% early-payment discount under Florida law . The discount falls to 3% in December, 2% in January and 1% in February, with the full amount due in March. Unpaid bills generally become delinquent April 1. Under the office’s existing rules, discounts are based on the date a payment is submitted online or in person. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Trump Media (DJT) Pledges 73% of Its Bitcoin to an Options Program as $1 Billion Note Deadline Nears Trump Media & Technology Group has pledged about 73% of its bitcoin to an options program in which the counterparty can reuse the coins, the company disclosed in its third-quarter 10-Q filed Monday, three weeks before holders of its $1 billion in convertible notes can demand cash. The Truth Social parent held approximately 15,649 BTC on Sept. 30, Chief Financial Officer Phillip Juhan said on Monday’s earnings call, along with 7 million shares of BlackRock’s IBIT. Of those coins, 11,385.20 were pledged to what the company calls its bitcoin yield management program. The filing says that program requires Trump Media to post bitcoin as collateral “that the counterparty can rehypothecate at their sole discretion.” The pledged coins carried a fair value of $951.4 million at quarter-end. The 10-Q does not name the counterparty. Another 4,260.73 BTC, worth $356.1 million on Sept. 30, sits as collateral for the convertible notes and cannot be withdrawn or distributed until the indenture’s conditions are met. Together, the two buckets account for about 15,646 BTC, nearly all of the stack Juhan described. How the Trump Media options program works Trump Media sells and buys covered calls and puts on bitcoin, settled in bitcoin, to “generate yield on these assets and increase our principal balance of bitcoin,” the filing says. Premiums arrive in bitcoin and are “immediately rehypothecated to our digital asset manager to reinvest.” At quarter-end it had written calls referencing 4,838.40 BTC at strikes from $68,000 to $92,000 and puts on 1,500 BTC at $75,000 to $80,000, all expiring in October. A risk factor spells out the trade-off. The company says its yield counterparties “may not be rated” by credit agencies, that it is limited in its ability to sell or use deployed bitcoin while the arrangements are open, and that where they are unsecured “we may be unable to recover deployed bitcoin in a counterparty insolvency.” Juhan said Trump Media bought 4,359 bitcoin during the quarter with proceeds from a partial sale of its IBIT position, part of a shift toward “third-party institutional” management of its treasury. A $409.7 million profit and a Nov. 30 deadline The bitcoin rally in the third quarter turned Trump Media profitable on paper. Danielle was crowned Miss Universe Nigeria 2026 on 27 September at the Balmoral Hall, Federal Palace Hotel in Lagos. Competing as Miss Lagos State against 19 other delegates, her victory marked a full-circle moment: her mother won the national title in 1991, 35 years before her. An alumnus of King’s College London, Danielle holds an MBBS alongside a first-class honours degree in Psychology. Alongside her medical career, she leads Scrub the Stigma, an initiative focused on expanding healthcare access and raising awareness around women’s health across Nigeria and the UK. Miss Universe Nigeria 2026 Danielle Adewusi wearing her official national crown and gold sequin gown. With recent updates by the Miss Universe Organisation removing maximum age limits, 29-year-old Danielle is also among the delegates competing under the expanded eligibility rules. Arriving in San Juan on Monday, 9 November, Danielle joins nearly 120 delegates from across the globe for preliminary rounds, national costume presentations, and rehearsals. The grand finale of the 75th Miss Universe pageant takes place on Tuesday, 24 November 2026, at the Coliseo de Puerto Rico José Miguel Agrelot in San Juan. entertainment.description: Skepta holding the official clear vinyl edition of his sixth studio album, The Fork and Knife. Photo Credit: Skepta/Instagram Your playlist could do with a little shake-up, and these five albums might be exactly what it needs. Skepta is reconnecting with his roots, Phyno is giving us more of the indigenous rap we love, Ty Bello has two albums exploring different expressions of worship, and Anendlessocean and Tobe Nwigwe are taking their sounds in interesting directions. From UK grime and Nigerian hip-hop to alternative gospel and soul, there’s a lot to discover across these new releases. Whether you’re in the mood for bars, worship, thoughtful songwriting or music that brings different cultures together, this week’s selection has something worth hearing. Skepta: The Fork & Knife Back in 2012, Skepta found himself at odds with a corporatised grime scene, sparking a pivotal career reckoning that eventually led to his landmark 2016 album Konnichiwa. On his long-awaited 15-track sixth album, The Fork & Knife, the 44-year-old MC reflects on his journey as grime’s most influential elder statesman and the son of Nigerian immigrants. Named after his mother’s favourite proverb, the record is a deep exploration of identity and perseverance. Musically, Skepta bridges continents by blending global diasporic sounds. He teams up with Aya Nakamura on the zouk-infused “ Chippie ”, taps Asake for the Afrobeats crossover “ Aloe Vera ”, and recruits Chase & Status alongside Suggs for the sharp single “ Innocent Smile ”. The project closes with “ Belly ”, an eight-minute masterclass featuring Boy Better Know members Jme and Frisco . ﻿ Phyno: Let That Sink In Arriving nearly 10 years after his groundbreaking sophomore record The Playmaker, Phyno’s 15-track sixth solo album, Let That Sink In (LTSI), showcases his timeless command of indigenous rap. The album features powerhouse collaborations, including Seyi Vibez on the opener “ Ndu Ka Aku ”, Fireboy DML on “ I Believe ”, and Jeriq on “ Ije Enu ”. Whether taking the government to task on “20 Years to Come” or offering uplifting anthems like “ Chukwu Okike ”, Phyno proves why he remains a definitive voice in African hip-hop. ﻿ Ty Bello: I Speak Lion and I Speak Lamb Creative powerhouse Ty Bello delivers a massive double-album listening experience with I Speak Lion and I Speak Lamb . entertainment.description: During Lagos Fashion Week, The Ladymaker ’s Founder and Creative Director, Ifeyinwa Azubike, introduced Stand On Ceremony, a collection that considers the relationship between personal expression and the expectations attached to an occasion. Presented on 27 October 2026 at The Sphere, Lagos, the collection draws from the familiar expression to stand on ceremony: to insist on the observance of formalities. For Ifeyinwa Azubike, the idea presents an opportunity to examine the traditions women inherit, the rituals they observe and the choices they make when dressing for themselves. The collection is built around two identities: The Devotee and The Rebel. They are not opposing personalities so much as two ways of relating to ceremony. The Devotee embraces its rituals. She understands the language of formal dressing and participates in it with intention. For her, dressing fully is an expression of desire and personal conviction. The Rebel is equally familiar with the rules, but she is selective about the ones she follows. Her approach to dressing allows for disruption, though never simply for the sake of attention. Through these characters, Azubike considers a familiar experience for women: the pull between what an occasion expects and what an individual wants to express. Every woman who has dressed for an occasion has encountered this tension in some form, whether in choosing to honour a tradition or finding room to express herself within it. The garments give form to this conversation. The Cloister Dress is paired with the Banner Dress, while the Manor Jumpsuit is placed alongside the Assembly Set. Other looks, including the Herald Dress, Emissary Set, Procession Dress and Sovereign Set, extend the collection’s exploration of the two identities. Material choices move between crimson jacquard, rose jacquard, ice jacquard, denim Akwete, wine Adire, midnight sequins and beaded velvet. The collection draws on fabrics and textures that allow ceremony to be interpreted through different moods, silhouettes and degrees of formality. Stand On Ceremony was presented during Lagos Fashion Week through an intimate fashion presentation, followed by a soirée where guests could experience the garments more closely. The evening was held in partnership with MAC Cosmetics, which provided beauty; Moët & Chandon, the champagne partner; Jacque Scents, which created the fragrance experience; and The Nail Boutique , responsible for nail artistry. For Ifeyinwa Azubike, the question the collection leaves with its audience is a personal one: are you a Rebel or a Devotee? entertainment.description: Africa’s tech icon and Chairman of Zinox Group , Leo Stan Ekeh , has told an international gathering of women leaders that his decision to build a technology company in Africa, at a time when the sector was virtually non-existent on the continent, amounted to what he described as “corporate suicide”. Speaking on the theme “Losing the Fear” , at The International Women Leadership Conference (TIWLC) in Dubai, organised by the Ibukun Awosika Leadership Foundation, Ekeh , who was a keynote speaker on the final day of this year’s conference, addressed over 600 women industry leaders from different countries across the globe. He said he returned from his studies abroad to a Nigeria where his peers were filing into banking, oil and gas, and where technology was largely seen as a foreign game. Ekeh, who studied Economics in India, said he was discouraged from pursuing a postgraduate degree in Computer Science in Europe because of the prevailing perception then that Africa might have little need for computers over the next 35 years, potentially leaving him frustrated. He subsequently opted for a postgraduate degree in Risk Management before pursuing a Master’s degree in Business Law (LLM) at London Guildhall University. He recalled that he could not sit his final law examinations because he had diverted his tuition fees into his passion for technology entrepreneurship. He also disclosed that he had fended off recruitment attempts by international technology companies that had sought to hire him before his return to Africa. “I chose the road not taken,” he told the conference. “It was corporate suicide in the eyes of my parents and many others. I lost the fear because I believed technology was the master key that would unlock possibilities for Nigeria and Africa.” He said the journey came with considerable hardship, including living on one meal a day for over three years and sleeping in a very small room in his office. According to him, his vision was to create a Nigerian and, by extension, an African IT identity. Recalling the launch of his first company, Task Systems Ltd, over 35 years ago, the company that pioneered desktop publishing and computer graphics in Nigeria. At the launch, held at the Sheraton Hotel, Ikeja, Ekeh recalled addressing an overcrowded hall filled with industry leaders, some of whom were seeing computers for the first time. He told them: “No country can claim to be independent without technology independence.” He said the Nigerian media embraced the vision, describing him as a “miracle child” and supporting the company’s roadmap. This, he noted, contributed to the computerisation of over 97 per cent of media and multimedia houses in Nigeria, as well as in other African countries. entertainment.title: Nkanyeziyethu Malunga: The Zimbabwean Designer Preserving African Heritage Through Fashion
entertainment.description: At her workshop in Bulawayo, Zimbabwe, Nkanyeziyethu Malunga crafted colour into fabric, using plants, tree bark and other natural materials gathered from the environment. Choosing a colour or designing a pattern is only one of the processes. Each material carries details on how it was gathered, prepared, and transformed, which Malunga is incorporating into contemporary fashion. “My dyes are mainly extracted from plants such as mnyii and hibiscus. Although I also use many other plants, including tubers, that have properties suitable for dye extraction. I love hibiscus not only for its petals, which produce beautiful dyes, but also for its tea.” The 37-year-old designer is challenging conventional notions about what defines a fashion collection and where creative knowledge originates. Through her clothing business, GANU, she transforms indigenous materials and skills into clothes and accessories, demonstrating how knowledge passed down through generations can inform modern design, provide opportunities for rural women, and conserve cultural practices. Her method is based on teachings learned from her late maternal grandmother, Ngatsha Nkatha, who resided in Tsholotsho, a rural district in Zimbabwe. During the school vacations, Malunga and her siblings traveled from Bulawayo to visit grandma, witnessing as she turned sisal, sedge, and reeds into winnowing baskets. “When I was a child, I often visited my grandmother in the village with my siblings. She was very dexterous with her fingers, and that passion eventually became mutual.” Malunga started experimenting with fashion in her teens before launching Ganu in 2013. The name is derived from iganu, the Ndebele term for marula fruit, and represents her connection to local resources and African identity. Her creations blend basketry, crocheting, batik, and beadwork with natural dyes, leather, and other locally produced materials. For Malunga, the importance of these materials goes beyond their appearance. sports.title: Grade the trade: Vikings get a throwback QB, deal with Raiders for old friend Kirk Cousins
sports.description: After Monday night, the Minnesota Vikings knew they had to try to get a quarterback. They landed a familiar face. The Vikings traded for Kirk Cousins, who spent six of his 15 NFL seasons in Minnesota. They sent a third-round pick to the Raiders for the 38-year-old quarterback, via ESPN . That should start the Fernando Mendoza era in Las Vegas, while giving the Vikings hope for fixing their offense and winning the NFC North. Here are the grades for the trade: Vikings trade for Kirk Cousins Usually, viable quarterbacks aren’t available in trade. Credit to the Vikings for getting a deal done. After Minnesota watched Carson Wentz flounder around on Monday night, and after the team realized Kyler Murray wouldn’t be the answer, a bold move was needed. Cousins has played pretty well this season, with 20 touchdowns and eight interceptions. He can come right in and run Kevin O’Connell’s offense, which made him more valuable to Minnesota than some other teams. Kirk Cousins is coming back to the Vikings for a second stint with the team. (Photo by Thearon W. Henderson/Getty Images) Thearon W. Henderson via Getty Images The Vikings weren’t going to be a Super Bowl contender with a treacherous quarterback situation. Cousins might not completely change that — he’s still by far the fourth-best quarterback in a tough division — but it’s well worth the price of a third-round pick to find out. Grade: B Raiders get a valuable pick The Raiders played the Kirk Cousins/Fernando Mendoza situation perfectly, as it turns out. They paid Cousins and gave him the first nine games of the season. sports.title: Video catches USC announcer's take on targeting call
sports.description: He said what? That’s what many were asking regarding longtime USC football radio play-by-play announcer Pete Arbogast’s reaction to Oregon quarterback Dante Moore being knocked out of Saturday’s 41-27 Ducks’ victory at Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum. The play occurred in the second quarter when Moore scrambled and slid. USC linebacker Desman Stephens II then put his shoulder into Moore’s head, knocking him backward into the turf. Moore lay on the field for several minutes before being taken off on a cart and loaded into an ambulance. Stephens celebrated the hit even after being flagged, leading to a skirmish with several Oregon players. Meanwhile, up in the radio booth, Arbogast said the play did not appear to be targeting and claimed Moore didn’t slide feet-first. Arbogast went on to claim that Stephens went in helmet first and ran into Moore who “ducked into that hit.” “I saw him dive forward,” Arbogast claimed. Radio analyst Shaun Cody, who played defensive line at USC (2001-2004) and spent eight seasons in the NFL (Detroit and Houston), clearly disagreed. “He’s laying feet first,” Cody responded. But Arbogast countered, “Well, he is now because they spun him around.” Cody disagreed again, and Arbogast said he wanted to see the replay, which clearly showed Moore sliding feet-first and Stephens going in head-first, with his right shoulder striking Moore in the head. “Yeah, not a feet-first slide, it’s more of a knee slide,” Arbogast claimed while watching the replay. While it’s one thing not to see clearly a live play from high up in a radio booth, it’s another to watch the replay and claim to see something that didn’t exist. Footage from the USC radio team in the Oregon game 😂😂😂 i can’t believe this is real pic.twitter.com/82HYans8Y9 — Adam Breneman (@AdamBreneman81) September 29, 2026 Cody immediately smirked at Arbogast’s viewpoint; then Arbogast added, “It didn’t look like targeting on the replay to us.” In response, Cody looked directly into the camera, eyes wide, and nodded, clearly disagreeing with Arbogast’s assessment. Homerism? Maybe. Potential advertising fodder for local optometrists to encourage thousands to update their eyeglass prescriptions? Absolutely. Oregon backup quarterback Dylan Raiola replaced Moore and passed for 289 yards and two touchdowns in the win. Moore was later diagnosed with a concussion; he has entered concussion protocol and will be out indefinitely . Moore released a statement saying he would soon return. Utah and “the Jazz.” Once, there was even Detlef Schrempf and a headband, if you can believe that. Ja Morant and Damian Lillard? We’re about to find out if they belong on such a list. Heck, the Blazers’ most valuable point guard last season was forward Deni Avdija. “I’m sure there will be questions about fit,” General Manager Joe Cronin said Monday. Uh, yeah. The Blazers have little more than three weeks before the regular season begins in which to figure that out. At the team’s annual media day on Monday, Morant appeared in a fresh white No. 1 Trail Blazers jersey. sports.description: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images The Philadelphia 76ers have won every single close game they have played this season, but that perfect record might be the biggest problem they face. The team improved to 9-2 on the season after beating the Chicago Bulls 127-121 on Sunday, a victory that kept their clutch record at a flawless 8-0. While fans love the drama, the reality is that a roster full of aging stars cannot survive this much stress week after week. The 76ers have played eight clutch games so far, which is the most in the entire league by a wide margin, according to The Sixer Sense . LeBron James has a clear explanation for why the team stays cool when the clock winds down. He told reporters after the win that the squad simply does not panic under pressure. “We have a lot of guys that’s been in late-game situations, and we have a no-panic button,” James said. He added that the group understands they must get stops, but they also know how to stay calm if the other team goes on a run. This mindset has worked so far, but it masks a deeper issue with how the team plays for the full 48 minutes. The Danger of Constant Comebacks Winning tight games is a great trait to have, yet relying on it every night is a recipe for exhaustion. According to The Sixer Sense , the 76ers have recovered from deficits to secure victories far too frequently this season, even versus inferior opponents. A team that does not dominate early will eventually run out of gas, and this roster is not exactly young across the board. Although the 76ers must leverage their talent edge earlier, they repeatedly allow contests to reach the last possessions for a winner to emerge. This pattern is dangerous for a group that includes players like James and Joel Embiid who need rest. Shooting Stars in the Final Minutes The stats show just how well the offense clicks when the pressure is highest. In clutch time, the Sixers are outscoring opponents 86-67 while shooting 52.2% from the field, according to Crossing Broad. Tyrese Maxey contributed significantly to that success by recording 30 clutch points on 6-of-11 shooting plus 15-of-17 from the line with no turnovers. LeBron James also contributed 22 points in the win over the Bulls, marking his highest-scoring game as a 76er. Even though the numbers look great, the fact remains that they should not need to rely on such high-pressure finishes to get Ws. The 76ers will need to find a way to start strong and keep that level of play for the whole game if they want to avoid burning out. The team has the firepower to put away opponents early, yet they keep finding themselves in tense moments when their talent suggests they should be winning by double digits. Now 8-0 in games extending to crunch time, the 76ers possess a perfect record that remains notable despite growing clarity about the dangers of this strategy.

sports.title: Here’s What Malik Nabers Revealed After Fox Criticized His Attitude
sports.description: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images New York Giants wide receiver Malik Nabers has entered a heated public dispute with Fox Sports broadcasters following the team’s 19-11 victory over the Philadelphia Eagles on Sunday. During the game, play-by-play announcer Joe Davis and analyst Greg Olsen criticized Nabers for his demeanor, with Davis stating the player’s body language “has been terrible today”. Nabers responded quickly on social media, taking to an Instagram story to call out the commentators for their assessment. Defending the Stoic Look The core of the argument centers on whether a player must show emotion to be a good teammate. Olsen had suggested that great receivers must demand the ball, noting, “There’s never been a great wide receiver who hasn’t demanded the ball”, according to ESPN . However, he also warned that being demanding should never hurt the team’s success. Nabers rejected the idea that his face changes based on the score. He insisted, “My face is the same way if I’m having a good game, bad, winning or losing”. Nabers clarified that his frustration was actually directed at his own team’s effort, not his teammates. He admitted he felt the offense was “lollygagging our way through the game”, according to Sports Illustrated . He explained that he was trying to “wake everybody up just to make sure we’re playing a game right now”. The receiver emphasized that in a division matchup, players must “go attack people, you have to go attack the game”. Coach Harbaugh Steps In Giants head coach John Harbaugh addressed the controversy during his media availability on Monday. He defended his player, pointing out that outsiders cannot see the full context of what happens on the field. Harbaugh asked, “If you really don’t know the person, or you don’t know the dynamic or you don’t know the circumstances or who the person’s talking to, how do you have any idea what the application is and how do you judge it?” The coach concluded that it is difficult for anyone outside the huddle to make a fair call on player behavior. He stated simply, “It’s really hard to make a judgment on it”. Stats and Next Steps He finished the game with five receptions for 43 yards. The 2024 rookie set franchise records with 109 receptions in his first season. He also earned Pro Bowl honors that same year before tearing his right ACL in September 2025. Eight games into this year, Nabers has tallied 648 yards along with two touchdowns. The Giants host the Washington Commanders after winning their division. The next game is scheduled for Thursday, Nov. 12, at 8:15 p.m. ET at MetLife Stadium.

technology.title: 14-year-old creates tool for AI agents to band together like a team
technology.description: Built by a 14-year-old developer, a new tool called Autark treats AI agents as a virtual team that can work without constant prompting. Users put tasks in an inbox, where a manager agent delegates them to other agents that carry out the work and report their results. Agents can also ask clarifying questions if tasks are too vague. “Agents do not wait for a prompt,” Autark’s website explains . “A schedule, a timer, a new task, a message or an event wakes them up. They decide what to do, do it, and can plan their own next step.” As one would hope from a product like this, Autark is model agnostic and can be set up to connect to OpenAI Codex, Claude Code, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, and Kimi Code through those services’ CLI tools. Local models are also supported. Your mileage may vary if you choose to use anything besides Codex or Claude Code, though, as Autark’s website mentions support for other models is built in but hasn’t been tested in a live run yet, as Autark is still under active development as an open-source tool. Real teenage engineering Autark is the brainchild of teenage Austrian developer Stanislaus Hees. He’s still in school, and tells The Register he’s deeply interested in AI and came up with Autark after being unhappy with existing AI tools. “I could get help with individual tasks, but I still had to organise the work, remember what was unfinished and keep pushing it forward,” Hees said of his time using Claude Code and Codex. “I wanted a system that could take responsibility for ongoing work, not just respond to my next message.” He developed Autark - or, more accurately, prompted AI coding tools to do it for him - to come up with a tool that could fulfill that want. You know what that means: It’s capable, but that capability also makes it dangerous. Autark’s page on access and data makes clear what’s at risk if you give it unfettered access to a PC, and why you don’t want to let the thing run roughshod over a system. “It can do everything,” the page explains , because “Autark does not put walls around its agents.” There’s no sandboxing in Autark, no approval prompts, and no permission gates. It doesn’t stop agents from spending all the money they can get their hands on, deleting files, or sending unsolicited emails, either. Agents run with the privileges of the machine's user, with approval checks and permission restrictions disabled or bypassed. Even the safety limit parley that users have with Autark establishes guidelines, not rules. “The first thing the AI asks is how far it may go,” the access page points out. “That is a question, not a technical barrier.” That means agents given a task that conflicts with their stated limits may still attempt to carry it out. technology.title: Mozilla Thunderbird email service edges closer to launch with early access
technology.description: The Mozilla-backed Thunderbird project is getting closer to a wider launch of a hosted email service designed to complement its desktop mail app. Now known as Thundermail (what else?), the service was originally developed under the Thunderbird Pro banner, which encompassed paid email, appointment scheduling, and file-sharing services designed to generate additional revenue for the organization. The org has been inviting people from its Thundermail waitlist to try the service through an early-access program, and this writer just happened to be among them. Thundermail offers a web-based email interface and can also be accessed through the Thunderbird desktop app, the Thunderbird mobile app for Android, or other compatible email clients. The Thunderbird apps remain free. Users get an inbox with up to 15 email addresses and three custom domains, plus 30 GB of mail storage and 60 GB of send storage for Thunderbird Send, an end-to-end encrypted file-sharing and large-attachment service. That’s for starters – the org intends to offer those extra features and services at different price points. Yes, Thundermail is a paid service, which may put off some users who are used to free email accounts offered via Gmail, Outlook.com and Proton Mail, but with the first two of those you do get served ads along with your messages. The sign-up screens for Thundermail suggest the basic service will cost $6 per month, billed annually. This is roughly equivalent to the £55 we paid for a year on the early access program. We asked Thunderbird when we can expect to see Thundermail officially launched and open to all comers. We will update if we get an answer. It previously said that a full launch is expected sometime in 2026. The web-based user interface of Thundermail presents a fairly clean and uncluttered look, and could be likened to Gmail with the screen partitioned into a pane with folders on the left and a larger one to the right displaying messages. A welcome screen introduces you to the features of Thundermail, which include the ability to work on several drafts at once, schedule delivery times for emails, create folders to arrange messages, contact lists and identities – all pretty much standard for an email system. We haven’t really had the time to test out Thundermail a great deal since signing up, but there are no great surprises so far, and everything works pretty much the way you would expect it to. Firefox and the Thunderbird mail client both recently moved to a fortnightly release schedule in line with Mozilla’s plans, and Thunderbird itself gained support for Microsoft’s Exchange late last year. ®

technology.title: AMD winds up Zen 6 cores for faster clock speeds
technology.description: After teasing its 256-core Epycs for more than a year, AMD is finally ready to talk about architectural changes to the Zen core that not only make it possible, but will eventually power its next generation of Ryzen processors in desktop and mobile PCs. During a press event in Las Vegas last week, AMD spilled the beans on its latest Zen cores, which promise an average 27 percent uplift in instructions per clock (IPC) across a variety of AI and server workloads, along with boosted clocks ranging from 4.1 to 5.3 GHz. We expect to see even higher frequencies on consumer chips before long, but AMD isn’t quite ready to talk about Ryzen just yet. CPU performance is a function of power, IPC, and clocks, and with gains across all three, the cores are shaping up to be one of the company’s biggest generational jumps ever. A tale of two cores As in past Epyc launches, Zen 6 isn’t one core. It comes in two flavors: a frequency-optimized variant (Zen 6) and a density-optimized version (Zen 6c). This split dates back to the launch of AMD’s Bergamo Epycs in 2023, which packed 128 compact Zen 4c cores into just eight chiplets. The chip’s debut drew comparisons to Intel’s still relatively new Efficient (E-cores) for obvious reasons. But under the hood, AMD’s Zen 4c was nothing like what Intel was doing. The core itself was nearly identical to Zen 4; it simply traded clocks and a bit of cache per core for a more densely packed CPU die. The only difference between running an application on Bergamo or Genoa was how quickly it executed. The same could not be said of Intel’s P and E cores, which used different ISAs. This remained a defining characteristic and advantage of AMD’s compact core architecture through Zen 5, which allowed it to ship Turin parts with up to 192 cores without users having to worry about whether their app was running on a compact core or not. With Zen 6c, at least as we understand it, this philosophy is largely unchanged. Both Zen 6 and Zen 6c share the same ISA, with clock being the main differentiator. There are other micro-architectural differences between the two cores designed to balance IPC and clock speeds more effectively. Looking at the core’s block diagram, this isn’t immediately obvious. Zen 6 and Zen 5 share a very similar front and backend. We'd be tempted to call the core iterative if it weren't for the 20 to 31 percent IPC uplift for cloud and AI workloads that AMD claims over Zen 5. This suggests that core for core, a 4.1 GHz Zen 6c-based Venice Epyc should deliver performance on par with a Zen 5-based Turin Epyc running at 5 GHz. That's a pretty sizable jump, but just because AMD is seeing generational performance uplift in enterprise server and cloud workloads doesn't mean we'll see the same gains on the client side. science.title: Uranus has a weird magnetic field that's stumped scientists for 40 years — we may finally know why
science.description: The posided magnetic fields of Uranus and Neptune may stem from extreme conditions lying within their deep interior. Unravelling the mystery behind the magnetic fields of these worlds is giving us new insight into the little-known interiors of the ice giants. Only one spacecraft has ever visited Uranus and Neptune, the Voyager 2 spacecraft which spend past Uranus in January 1986 and Neptune in August 1989. Voyager 2 found that their planetary magnetic fields were, to put it bluntly, wonky. Uranus’ magnetic field was offset from its rotational axis by 59 degrees and isn’t even centered on the planet’s core, but instead is only two-thirds of the way down. Neptune is similar, with a disordered magnetic field offset by 47 degrees and centered halfway between the core and its visible cloud tops. If we compare these planets to Earth , which has a stable magnetic field tilted by just 11 degrees to our planet’s rotation, we can see how extreme the magnetic fields of the ice giants are. Various explanations for the strange magnetic fields of the ice giants have been put forward over the years. Uranus as a whole is tilted by 97 degrees and effectively rolls around the sun , and speculation is that billions of years ago it was knocked on its side by a collision with a long-lost Earth-sized planet. Could this collision have also skewed its magnetic field? This might be a plausible explanation were Neptune’s magnetic field also not similarly skewed without having experienced a collision. Clearly, whatever the cause, it must be intrinsic to the nature of the two ice giant planets. Now, a new study by scientists in the U.S. and the UK, based on computer simulations and Voyager 2’s measurements of the two planets’ magnetic fields, may have found a solution. The solution to the weird magnetic fields of the solar system's ice giants may come down to how planets generate their magnetic field through the dynamo effect. This arises from the swirling, convective motion of an electrically conducting liquid within a rotating body, which is able to generate and maintain a powerful magnetic field. Inside Earth, the electrically conducting fluid is the molten iron in the outer part of our planet’s core, and the magnetic field that it generates has clear north and south poles – what we call a dipole, a phenomenon that we can also see in the two magnetic poles of a simple bar magnet. However, the conditions inside Uranus and Neptune are somewhat different. As ice giants, they contain a lot of volatiles – ammonia, hydrogen, helium, methane, and water surrounding a probable rocky core. Furthermore, Uranus and Neptune are substantially larger than Earth , with 14.5 and 17 times the mass of our planet, respectively. This increased mass creates crushing conditions within the interior of the ice giants. Micah Hanks is a science reporter and podcaster focusing on space and astronomy, and Editor at TheDebrief.org. Follow him on X @MicahHanks.

In the final weeks of 1960, two young radio enthusiasts were monitoring transmissions from a home-built listening station on a rooftop in Turin, Italy, when the brothers detected something extraordinary: a faint signal that bore the hallmarks of one originating from space. That wasn't the only surprising thing about the alleged signal:, the transmission carried a very familiar message: it was Morse code for the international distress signal SOS. As the youths listened, the signal seemed to grow weaker. This raised a troubling possibility: could it be that the signal's source was moving farther away from Earth ? And if so, was it possible that this concerning signal was of Soviet origin — perhaps a spacecraft drifting helplessly into space, carrying a cosmonaut on board whose doomed mission had never been publicly acknowledged? These strange events from November 1960 became the first in a series of alleged radio signal interceptions that would form the basis of an enduring Cold War-era mystery involving so-called "lost cosmonauts" — early Soviet space travelers rumored to have died during secret spaceflight missions before Yuri Gagarin's historic flight the following spring, in April 1961.Today, more than six decades later, the story remains one of the most haunting legends of the Space Age. Were there truly early Soviet space missions — with tragically ill-fated cosmonaut crews — that remain undisclosed to this day? Interception at Torre Bert The peculiar story began in October 1957, as the Italian brothers Achille and Gian Battista Judica-Cordiglia learned, along with the rest of the world, about the Soviet Union's successful launch of Sputnik 1 , Earth's first artificial satellite. Immediately, the two became fascinated with the idea of trying to listen in on signals from such spacecraft and began working to assemble their very own radio tracking station, which they put together mostly from secondhand military surplus equipment. What they couldn't easily find and purchase, the brothers would often assemble themselves. They built an improvised tracking station in an abandoned World War Two bunker , which the brothers dubbed Torre Bert, that eventually became a fully functional radio facility with an antenna they built from salvaged materials like chicken wire and scraps of metal.
